title: This Newt Stabs Attackers With Its Own Ribs, Through Its Own Skin

scenes.text: Grab this newt and it stabs you. With its ribs.
The Spanish ribbed newt looks harmless. Then something bites it.
It swings its ribs forward by up to 50 degrees, until the sharp tips burst out through its own skin.
At the same moment it oozes a milky poison over its body. The ribs push through it like dipped needles.
Every time it does this, the bones break through the body wall again. The newt barely seems to notice.
It is immune to its own poison, and its skin heals over. So, who wants to pick it up?

description:
A newt that stabs attackers with its own ribs, pushed straight through its own skin.
When threatened, the Spanish ribbed newt rotates its ribs forward by up to 50 degrees until the sharp tips pierce the body wall, while secreting a milky poison over its skin, so the rib tips work like poison-dipped needles. The bones break through the skin each time the defense is triggered, yet the newt suffers no lasting harm: it is immune to its own toxin and its skin heals (Journal of Zoology, University of Vienna, 2009).
Which animal has the strangest self-defense you know?

first_comment: A researcher who has handled them says the ribs feel like small needles, and the reflex is to let go, which is the whole point. Which animal would you least like to grab?
